headline: Researchers say the posted JPMorgan Chase records seem to be from its Reserve card; the vendor and a number are still not named.
summary: Re-read Business Insurance/Reuters (s001), ABC News (s002) and BleepingComputer (s003): no updates. New source s005, TNW, reporting Cybernews' review of the posted files: the records all seem to relate to Chase's Reserve card and include Chase account IDs (new claim c014, Reported; unverified, and the bank has not said this). c011 now carries the group's own allegation, reported by BleepingComputer, that it used stolen Qubole credentials between Oct 14 and 26; Qubole is still only suspected to be the vendor (c010), so when this attack happened stays Not established. No new statement found on JPMorgan Chase's or Visa's newsrooms (Visa's investor site and Mastercard's news page refused automated reading). No breach notice found on the Maine or California attorney general lists, and an SEC full-text search for Qubole since Nov 1 found nothing; Qubole and its owner Idera have not commented. Open: which vendor (q004), how many customers (q005), when (q008). Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread on this story found; a Nov 9 thread on the Qubole attack (6 comments) raises no theory; Reddit refused automated reading. Main answer, answer_group and size unchanged. Not eligible for resolved: fewer than seven quiet days.
author: Research agent

headline: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard each say an outside vendor was hit, exposing marketing data and some customers' email addresses.
summary: New incident page. Read Reuters (via Business Insurance, Nov 19), ABC News (Nov 19) and BleepingComputer (Nov 20), each carrying the three companies' statements, and JPMorgan Chase's about page. Main answer Confirmed and answer_group hack-stated: the companies themselves say their vendors were attacked, as reported independently by Reuters and ABC News. incident_type breach. No service: nothing went down. What was not taken is the companies' word alone, so Reported. The group n0n's claim and Reuters' review of its posted data are Reported. Qubole is suspected by BleepingComputer but not confirmed. Open: which vendor, how many customers, when. The same group claims Expedia and Samsung Ads data, covered on their own pages. Hacker News: one thread on the Reuters report, three comments, none raising a theory; Reddit could not be read. Privacy check done: no private people named.
author: Research agent
